meta: Dramas like While You Were Sleeping: six kind supernatural mysteries where decency is the actual subject.
standfirst: Dreams that show a crime before it happens, a prosecutor who has to act on them without evidence, and a show whose real subject is people choosing to intervene. The pleasure is not the mystery, it is the decency: three neighbours who keep deciding to do the harder thing. These six sit near that, and we say which ones keep the kindness and which trade it for tension.

picks.why: Same writer, same director, same faith in ordinary goodness. Park Hye Ryun and Oh Choong Hwan together again, on a girl who spends fifteen years on an island and comes back wanting to sing, and the show's engine is a household of people quietly protecting each other. Park Eun Bin is the reason to watch. Difference: it fumbles the move to Seoul badly, and the abuse plot it takes on is heavier than anything here.

The same premise with the ability moved to touch. A young man reads memories by contact and chases a building collapse everyone involved is lying about, using the gimmick to withhold context rather than hand over answers. Same mix of warm ensemble and cold institutional cover-up, and the per-episode ratings climb to 9.6 by the finale. Difference: the trauma is personal and specific to the leads, so the tone is more melancholy and much less funny.

Lee Jong Suk in the version with the throttle wide open. A surgeon pulled inside her father's webtoon, a hero who works out he is written, and four opening episodes with more invention than most shows manage in sixteen. Same appetite for a rule that reshapes the plot. Difference: it is a thriller with real violence in it, and the back half breaks its own rules where this one keeps them.

If the courtroom half was what held you. Cold cases solved across a twenty year radio link, plotted more tightly than anything else on the site, and driven by the same idea: knowing a crime is coming and having no admissible way to prove it. Difference: nobody falls in love, and the institution is the antagonist rather than the workplace.

Same director, supernatural romance turned up to full volume. Oh Choong Hwan shooting a hotel for ghosts with the most confident visual language of his career, and the same structure of episodic cases inside a long romance. Difference: the Hong sisters wrote it, so the wit is sharper and the sentiment is bigger, and the male lead is the only reasonable person in the building.

A crime that arrives by phone, and no filler at all. A kidnapping call, a contract marriage and twelve episodes that move faster than a romance drama has any right to, with the sign language premise genuinely used. Same shape of a couple solving a case they are personally inside. Difference: the tone is cold thriller rather than gentle, and its final hour resolves things that never needed resolving.

against.title: Vagabond
against.why: Recommended off Bae Suzy and the conspiracy framing. It is an action thriller with a body count, a plot that treats characters as pieces, and an ending that exists to set up a second season nobody made. None of what makes While You Were Sleeping pleasant survives the swap.

against.title: Alice
against.why: The other Suzy science-fiction mystery, and the recommendation lands purely on that. It is a grief story wearing a thriller's clothes, cold where this is warm, and it spends its runtime explaining a machine rather than watching people choose.

against.title: The Girl Who Sees Smells
against.why: The obvious sibling on paper: one gifted sense, one serial killer, one romance. The tonal management is nowhere near it. The comedy and the murders sit in separate shows, and the killer is a cartoon where this one keeps its threat mundane and legal.
